title: Go: Generics
description: Use Go 1.18+ generics — type parameters, generic types, constraints, and comparable.

steps.title: Generic function with T any
steps.description: Write a generic function `Print[T any](v T)` that prints "Value: <v>" using fmt.Println. Call it with an int, a string, and a float64.

verification.successMessage: Generic function works with multiple types!
verification.failureMessage: Use [T any] syntax in the function signature.

steps.title: Generic type (List[T])
steps.description: Define a generic `List[T any]` struct with a `data []T` field. Add methods `Add(v T)` and `Get(index int) T`. Create a List[int], add 3 values, and print them via Get.

verification.successMessage: Generic List type works with methods!
verification.failureMessage: Define methods with the [T] type parameter on the receiver.

steps.title: Type constraints (interface)
steps.description: Define a `Number` constraint interface with `int | float64`. Write a generic `Sum[T Number](values []T) T` function that sums a slice. Call it with both `[]int{1,2,3}` and `[]float64{1.1, 2.2, 3.3}`.
hints: This is a type constraint interface — also called a union
The function can use + operator because the constraint allows it

verification.successMessage: Type constraints restrict and enable operations!
verification.failureMessage: Define the Number constraint interface with int | float64.

steps.title: Comparable constraint
steps.description: Write a generic function `Contains[T comparable](slice []T, val T) bool` that returns true if val is in the slice. Test with ints and strings and print the results.
hints: `comparable` is a built-in constraint for types that support == and !=
Use range to iterate over the slice

steps.title: Multiple type params
steps.description: Write a generic function `Pair[K comparable, V any](key K, value V) string` that formats and returns `"<key>: <value>"`. Call it with different key/value types and print the results.
hints: Syntax: `func Pair[K comparable, V any](k K, v V) string`

verification.successMessage: Multiple type parameters give maximum flexibility!
verification.failureMessage: Use fmt.Sprintf with %v to format different types.
